items.title: Leslie Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: I’m so excited about what Dave Robinson is doing

ctx.x: It was something that was started by a guy named John Bartles in Milwaukee. And it was — I want to say it was the late seventies, maybe ’78 or so, ’79. And John really had a vision that was exactly what you’re talking about. And he put on two — I believe it was two events — called the Milwaukee Jazz Experience. And I participated in it and Butch Thompson participated in it, a guy named Reggie Buckner who was the head of jazz

studies at the University of Minnesota was part of it, and what John accomplished is he got the superintendent of schools in Milwaukee to cooperate with him and they — and the Milwaukee Journal — for a whole year they prepared kids for the Milwaukee Jazz Experience which happened — it was still during the school year, the end of the school year. And the Milwaukee Journal published tabloids, not real thick, but tabloids about — it had a timeline, a historical timeline of jazz, and it had capsule histories of the…

Oh yeah. Right. ‘Cause young kids won’t be — I mean I think sometimes the problem with presenting this music is the audio quality of some of the original recordings. It just sounds too different to their ears.
